analysis.title: International Market Intelligence - Morning Briefing (November 9, 2026)
key_insights: JPM's flatter geopolitical risk curve is tracking, which the desk calls a positive for European and International equities.
Midterms could mean three things for markets: a flatter geopolitical risk curve in 2027, data-centre constraints, and greater fiscal discipline with some realignment toward the political centre.

Data-centre projects in 2027 may face fewer challenges, but the 2028-29 pipeline could face greater uncertainty. State-level regulatory uncertainty is a downside risk to consensus earnings for data-centre enablers. Capacity can move to friendlier US states, Canada, the Nordics or Spain, and some concerns are already priced in.

The shift from FOGO to capitulation seems to have happened and momentum longs have outperformed globally. Rock-bottom sentiment, short-term alpha drawdowns and a reset in momentum/semis exposure are tailwinds for a tradable bounce.

The desk still thinks thematic focus should remain in non-AI too. The Asia Strategy team agrees and suggests a diversified portfolio exposed to both a possible sharp AI-stock recovery and uncorrelated emerging opportunities.
APAC markets and US/EU futures are higher. Weaker oil after Trump signalled further airstrikes won't be necessary, plus capital markets news, are described as tailwinds.

Russia and Ukraine envoys discuss territorial issues and ceasefire-monitoring proposals at trilateral talks in Abu Dhabi. The desk's indicators show an improving narrative but do not yet discount a breakthrough.

Equity Strategy: the next stage of beta rotation depends on why bond yields have peaked. The team reiterates its early-October call that yields have peaked, stays with the Broadening call, and does not think AI is a continued sell. The peak in yields has instigated a rebound in Value vs Growth.
Asia Equity Strategy: AI stocks and Asian equity indices have broken below key technical levels, which threatens some knock-on volatility. The market looks oversold and positioning has lightened.

EMEA Metals & Mining: gold faces near-term headwinds from rates and energy uncertainty, but gold's resilience during Thursday's equity sell-off is encouraging and positioning in gold and silver is light. Midterm implications for the AI/data-centre buildout and refined copper tariffs are downside risks to copper, while tight Chinese supply should support prices.

EU Capital Goods: the de-rating across global electricals in recent weeks offers select buying opportunities. The group had traded at or above 1 std dev relative to its own 5-year averages into the summer. Bond markets set discount rates and AI regulation may curtail US data-centre growth.

Tactically bullish on Global Equities. The regional preference is long US and Asia (Japan, South Korea, Taiwan) versus EU, because the US is overheating, Europe is recovering from stagflation and secular themes carry less weight in EU equities.
Broadening can come back more clearly in the US than the EU. European earnings fundamentals are good and positioning gives a buy signal, but EU conviction needs stability in EGB spreads.

Positioning Intelligence: Multi-Strat de-grossing was the largest 20-day event since Covid, but long-short spreads improved last week. After the 20-day gross flow first fell below the 5th percentile (Oct. 27), alpha was higher over the next 20 days in 9 of 10 cases.

HF net leverage fell about 4% over the past week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low and global momentum exposure is near three-year lows. Semis remained the most net-sold US theme, and Defensives ex-Healthcare have begun to rebound.
Selling has not yet signaled broad capitulation. EMEA and China/HK saw net buying while North America and Japan saw net selling, and European short covering hit a 3z extreme last seen in late 2022.

vol_and_positioning: Multi-Strat 20-day gross flows fell below the 5th percentile on Oct. 27, the largest 20-day de-grossing since Covid. In 9 of 10 prior cases alpha was higher over the next 20 days.
HF net leverage fell about 4% in a week to near 12-month lows. Eq L/S net leverage is at a three-year low and All Strategy net leverage is around the 40th percentile on 3-/5-year bases.
Global momentum exposure is near three-year lows and close to neutral. APAC momentum exposure fell quickly from more extreme levels.
In the past five years HFs rebounded over the next 5 and 10 days in all eight comparable events with 5- and 20-day net returns below -2z.
European short covering reached a 3z extreme, last seen in late 2022.
Past midterm years most resemble 2022, when de-grossing continued into mid-month and gross flows recovered in December alongside a sell-off.
Option hedges: keep MCX < UKX until clarity on spending, pragmatism and ideology, and short FR vs EU Domestics on politics and dislocation.
